newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran paper accuses British diplomat of being spy.
newsitem.headline: Iran paper accuses British diplomat of being spy.

text.p: A hardline Iranian newspaper on Monday accused Britain's top diplomat in Tehran of being a member of the British intelligence agency MI6.

The daily Kayhan quoted an unnamed French diplomat as telling its sister weekly Kayhan Havai in Paris that Jeffrey James, charge d'affaires at the British embassy in Tehran, belonged to the MI6 Secret Intelligence Service.

The weekly quoted an unnamed informed source in Tehran as saying Iranian officials were investigating the case and that "it was possible that Iran would expel a British diplomat as persona non grata", Kayhan said.
British embassy officials in Tehran were not immediately available to comment.

The charges came amid a diplomatic row between Iran and the European Union after a German court accused Tehran leaders of ordering the 1992 killings of Kurdish dissidents in Berlin. Iran has denied involvement.

James was among EU envoys recalled for consultations after the April 10 verdict. A meeting of EU foreign ministers in Luxembourg last week suspended ministerial contacts with Iran but decided the envoys could return.

Iranian officials reacted to the EU decisions by saying Tehran would not allow the German ambassador to return to Tehran for now. Some newspapers quoted Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati as saying the same applied to the Danish envoy.
German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel on Monday blamed Iran for the row over the return of the ambassadors.
